As shown in figure, when a spherical cavity (centred at O) of radius 1 is cut out of a uniform sphere of radius R (centred at C), the centre of mass of remaining (shaded) part of sphere is at G, i.e. on the surface of the cavity. R can be determined by the equation (a) (R 2 +R+1)(2−R) = 1 (b) (R 2 +R−1)(2−R) = 1 (c) (R 2 −R−1)(2−R) = 1 (d) (R 2 −R+1)(2−R) = 1 [Figure: the cavity touches the sphere internally on the right, and G lies on the cavity's surface on the side away from O.]
